text: A refused D7.1 notice arrives as rwb.decision.ApprovalRefused.v1 and a returned one as rwb.decision.ApprovalReturned.v1 on rwb.decision.events.v1, one event per outcome, keyed by caseId, carrying the approval, the notice, the case, the final call, the reason or question and the record reference, and consumed by rwb-case with an inbox dedupe by event ID.
why: The slice must react to the outcome of the approval, and no source names the refusal or return event: the catalogue gives ApprovalRequested and the decision record only, so the consumed rows, the fakes and AC4 to AC6 need one stated name and payload.

impact: If P7 publishes one outcome event with a final-call attribute or other names, one consumed row, the NoticeOutcomeListener and two fixtures change; no schema, task or workflow change.

text: The redress task is one task row named by a task code held in reference data with its element type, owner role and due time, carries the notice and approval references in a task.notice_ref column and a reference field added by this story's migration, and one assignment row names recovery_case.owner_user_id as the assignee.
why: TSD P3 v3 gives the task table no notice or approval reference and no task code list, so the task cannot be written as the story needs it without one stated naming and one stated column.
read: TSD P3 v3 section T3.1 (task, assignment) and T3.2 (LOV-ELEMENT, LOV-TASK-STATUS, LOV-ROLE, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON); legacy RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 9 and AC3; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01, DP-07 and DP-15
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2014-APP s4 step 12, s11, s12.7, s13 (migration and reference data), AC4, AC5

impact: If the task code or the column differs, one migration column, one reference row, the RedressTaskService and two assertions change; the task, assignment and record writes stay the same.

text: The case facts are served under the existing API-P3-002 as a projection of caseNo, productGroup, stageCode, routeState, routeCode, status, ownerRef, entryDate, dpdAtEntry, totalOutstandingAtEntry, exposureBand and prescriptionDate with an inputAsOf array of inputCode, businessDate and ageDays per input, the two input codes being TOTAL_BALANCE and POSTAL_ADDRESS; the composite route takes businessDate and ageDays from this answer and limitDays and stale from rwb-decision's answer, so no limit is computed twice.
why: The panel must show each fact with the date it is true for and each input with its age, and neither the TSD response type names nor the legacy story give the field list or the age element, so the projection needs one stated shape.
read: TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-002 and API-P3-003, T3.1 recovery_case and case_account; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10; legacy RWB-E2-014 AC5 and AC10; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-13 and DP-19

impact: If the field list or the element differs, the CaseFactsProjection, the InputAgeService, one route mapping and the component fixtures change; the operations, the errors and the authorisation stay as they are.

text: rwb-case reads the current total balance and days past due at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{accountId} with data_as_of, the contact fact of the postal address input at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{customerId} for its business date only, and the ACE business date in force at GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, each one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and it reads no v_ace_* view itself.
why: The panel's facts and their ages come from ACE data, and the legacy story read them through v_ace_account and v_ace_contact inside one process; the target forbids that read, and no source gives the dated contact read or says which field carries the date.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 10; Ownership Map v1 api rows for P1 rwb-source-data; legacy RWB-E2-014 section 11 (DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-078); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05 and DP-11
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2014-APP s3, s4 steps 6 and 7, s11, s12.2, s12.8, s17, AC2, AC3, TC-E2-014-05
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 owner in the baseline review of RWB-P1-E1015-CON.
impact: If P1 publishes another path or another date field, one consumed row, the SourceDataClient and one fixture change; no event, schema or workflow change.

text: The interaction ledger stays rwb-source-data's under DP-18, so this story writes no ledger row: the refusal or return is recorded as the local decision record of DP-03 and appears on the case timeline as the decision item of rwb-decision's ledger read and the task item of task.
why: The legacy story wrote a decision entry in the same process as the task, and the target splits the record from the ledger while the case timeline needs both; no source says which service owns the item the panel shows.
read: Template and Rules R3 default rulings (interaction ledger owned by P1 rwb-source-data) and R5.5 DP-03, DP-18; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42; legacy RWB-E2-014 sections 11 and 12
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 and P7 owners at the ledger review, before the timeline read is published.
impact: If the ledger is read from another owner or the timeline item is composed elsewhere, the TimelineOutcomeAssembler and one consumed row change; the task write and the local record do not.

text: The Case record right and the scope of the caller are consumed at POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise on the RWB-P4-E1037-CON contract, cached for the life of the entry, refusing closed when the answer is missing, unparseable or unanswered, and this slice adds no guard library, permission row or masking row of its own.
why: The legacy story guarded the screen with RecoveryAccessGuard inside the monolith, and the assigned dependency set of this key carries no P4 contract story, so the authorise answer is consumed on the published contract as one hop with no DP-08 row in this slice.
